title: Smoked Brisket Baked Beans
equipment: Smoker or grill set up for indirect heat

items: 1½ bottles Heath Riles BBQ Sweet BBQ Sauce, divided (1 bottle and ½ bottle)
½ bag (1 lb, about 2¼ cups packed) Domino light brown sugar
⅓ yellow bell pepper, finely diced
⅓ red bell pepper, finely diced
⅓ green bell pepper, finely diced
1 lb leftover smoked Texas-style brisket, cut into ½-inch chunks
1 to 3 tbsp Heath Riles BBQ Hot BBQ Rub, to taste

steps: Heat your smoker to 275°F to 300°F for indirect cooking. You can also use your oven at the same temperature.
Nest one aluminum pan inside the other for support. Pour the drained beans into the top pan.
Add 1 bottle of the BBQ sauce. Spread the brown sugar over the top, breaking up any clumps with a spoon. Add the onion and all 3 bell peppers, then stir until the sugar is mixed in.

Add the brisket chunks and sprinkle on the rub, using more for hotter beans. Pour the remaining ½ bottle of sauce over everything and stir well. If making ahead, cover tightly with foil and refrigerate up to 1 day.
Set the pan uncovered on the smoker grate and close the lid. Cook until the beans start to bubble around the edges, about 45 min to 1 hr, then stir well.

Keep cooking, stirring every 30 min, for about 5 hr total. The beans are done when they're dark and thick with just a little liquid, the onions and peppers are tender, and the center reads at least 165°F. For soupier beans, stop at about 3 hr.
Remove the pan from the smoker and give the beans a final stir. Let them rest 10 min so the sauce thickens slightly, then serve.
tips: No brisket? Use 1 lb browned ground beef (cooked to 160°F) or leftover pulled pork instead.
If you only have green bell pepper, use 1 whole green pepper in place of the 3 partial peppers.
Go easy on the rub at first. You can add more near the end, but you can't take it out.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 3 days, or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat covered in a 325°F oven or in a pot over medium-low heat, stirring and adding a splash of water if thick, until hot throughout (165°F).
